oneLiner: 资产负债表拍“快照”、利润表记“一段成绩”、现金流量表看“真金白银的进出”。
oneLinerEn: The balance sheet is a snapshot, the income statement a season's score, the cash-flow statement the actual money in and out.
detail: 三者互相勾稽:利润按权责发生制计,不等于现金;企业可能账面盈利却因收不到钱而资金链断裂。读一家公司要把三张表连起来:赚不赚钱看利润表,家底与负债看资产负债表,钱从哪来、到哪去看现金流量表。
detailEn: The three tie together: accrual profit is not cash, and a firm can look profitable yet break its funding because it cannot collect. Read them as a set — profitability from the income statement, resources and debts from the balance sheet, and where money came from and went from the cash-flow statement.

oneLiner: 资产 = 负债 + 所有者权益——某一时点“有什么”必然等于“谁出的钱”。
oneLinerEn: Assets = liabilities + equity — at a point in time, what you have must equal who funded it.
detail: 一边的资产是资金的去向(现金、存货、设备),另一边是资金的来源(欠人的与股东自己的)。它像定格照片,回答偿债能力与资本结构;但历史成本计价、无形资产难以量化,使它并不等于“真实价值”。
detailEn: Assets are where the money went (cash, stock, equipment); the other side is where it came from — to creditors and to owners. A still photo answering solvency and capital-structure questions — yet historical cost and hard-to-value intangibles mean it is not 'true worth'.

oneLiner: 收入−成本−费用=利润,记录一段时间的经营成绩;但“利润”按权责发生制算,不等于收到现金。
oneLinerEn: Revenue minus cost and expenses equals profit over a period — but accrual 'profit' is not cash collected.
detail: 从营收一路减到毛利、营业利润、净利润,能看出钱花在哪、哪层利润被吃掉。关键是权责发生制:确认收入与费用的时点带来操纵空间(提前确认、递延费用)。所以利润表要和现金流量表对照着读。
detailEn: Stepping from revenue down to gross, operating and net profit shows where money goes and which layer is eaten. Accrual timing — when revenue and expense are recognised — leaves room to game it (pulling revenue forward, deferring cost), so read it against the cash-flow statement.

oneLiner: “现金为王”:利润是观点,现金是事实;经营、投资、筹资三条现金流讲清钱真正怎么转。
oneLinerEn: 'Cash is king': profit is an opinion, cash a fact — operating, investing and financing flows show how money really moves.
detail: 很多倒闭的企业账上有利润,却因现金枯竭而死。经营现金流衡量主业造血,投资现金流反映扩张或收缩,筹资现金流显示借新还旧或分红回购。三者的正负组合,比单一净利润更能揭示健康度。
detailEn: Many firms that failed were profitable on paper yet ran out of cash. Operating flow gauges the core business's self-funding, investing flow shows expansion or shrinkage, financing flow reveals borrowing, repaying, dividends and buybacks. Their signs together tell more about health than net profit alone.

oneLiner: 固定成本 ÷ 单位边际贡献 = 保本销量;越过它,每一单才开始赚钱。
oneLinerEn: Fixed cost divided by unit contribution gives the break-even volume; past it, each sale starts earning.
detail: 把成本拆成固定与变动,算出卖多少才能不亏,并评估降价、提量、控成本各自如何改变盈亏线。它简单有力,是定价与投产决策的入门工具;前提是能清晰划分固变动、且单价与成本在区间内相对稳定。
detailEn: Split cost into fixed and variable, compute the sales needed to lose nothing, and see how cutting price, lifting volume or trimming cost each shift the line. Simple but powerful for pricing and go/no-go calls — provided fixed and variable split cleanly and price and cost hold across the range.

oneLiner: 流动比率看偿债、负债率看杠杆、周转率看效率、毛利率看定价权。
oneLinerEn: Current ratio for solvency, leverage for debt, turnover for efficiency, margin for pricing power.
detail: 比率把绝对数标准化,便于跨期、跨公司比较;但单个比率意义有限,要横向(同业)、纵向(历年)、并拆开杜邦分解看驱动。滥用还会被“粉饰”——季末突击回款、把费用资本化,都能短期美化比率。
detailEn: Ratios normalise raw numbers for comparison across time and peers, yet no single one means much alone — read them against industry, history and a DuPont decomposition of drivers. They can also be dressed up: quarter-end collections and capitalising expense flatter them briefly.

oneLiner: 回报率把收益除以投入,让不同规模、不同项目能用同一把尺子比较。
oneLinerEn: Return over input lets projects and firms of different size be measured on one ruler.
detail: ROI = 净收益/投入,通用但口径易被操纵(时间、包含哪些成本);ROE = 净利/股东权益,衡量为股东赚钱的效率,杜邦把它拆成净利率×周转率×杠杆,一眼看出回报来自薄利、快转还是加杠杆。比较时务必对齐时间与定义。
detailEn: ROI is net gain over investment — universal but easy to game through the window chosen and which costs are counted; ROE is net profit over equity, and DuPont splits it into margin × turnover × leverage, exposing whether returns come from thin margins, fast turns or borrowed money. Always align the period and definitions when comparing.

oneLiner: 先算清“服务一个客户赚不赚”:客户终身价值要显著大于获客成本。
oneLinerEn: Before scaling, check one customer pays: lifetime value should clearly exceed the cost to acquire it.
detail: 互联网与订阅生意常亏损换增长,单位经济把“增长是否健康”量化:LTV(一个客户一生贡献的毛利)对 CAC(获取他的成本),健康线常取 LTV/CAC ≥ 3,并看多少回本周期。毛利、留存、复购任何一个变差,都会让规模越大亏越多。
detailEn: Consumer and subscription businesses often buy growth with losses; unit economics quantifies whether that growth is healthy — lifetime value (gross profit a customer yields over time) against customer-acquisition cost, a common rule of LTV/CAC at least 3 plus a payback period. Any slip in margin, retention or repeat purchase turns scale into a bigger hole.

oneLiner: 今天的一块钱比明天的一块钱值钱——折现把不同时点的现金流放到同一天比较。
oneLinerEn: A dollar today beats a dollar tomorrow — discounting brings cash flows at different times onto one date to compare.
detail: 因为钱可投资、有通胀与风险,未来金额要按贴现率折算成现值。净现值(NPV)把项目全部现金流折到今天再减投入,NPV > 0 才创造价值;内含报酬率(IRR)是令 NPV = 0 的贴现率。它是估值、资本预算与长期决策的地基。
detailEn: Because money earns and faces inflation and risk, future sums are discounted to present value. Net present value folds a project's whole cash stream to today minus the outlay — positive NPV creates value — and IRR is the rate that makes NPV zero. It is the ground under valuation, capital budgeting and long-horizon choices.

oneLiner: 别只盯财务——从财务、客户、内部流程、学习成长四个视角平衡地度量与驱动战略。
oneLinerEn: Look beyond finance — measure and steer strategy across four views: financial, customer, internal process, learning and growth.
detail: 卡普兰与诺顿(1992)提出:滞后、易被操纵的财务数字之外,还要有驱动未来绩效的领先指标(客户满意、流程质量、员工能力),并用“战略地图”把它们与财务结果串成因果链。它把口号般的战略翻译成可衡量的目标与行动。
detailEn: Kaplan and Norton (1992) argued that lagging, gameable financial numbers need leading indicators of future performance — customer satisfaction, process quality, staff capability — linked by a strategy map into a causal chain to financial results. It translates strategy-in-slogans into measured objectives and actions.

oneLiner: 流动资产减流动负债——够不够付近期的账，同时别让现金躺着不生息。
oneLinerEn: Current assets minus current liabilities — enough to pay near-term bills without letting cash sit idle.
detail: 营运资本管理的核心权衡是流动性与盈利性：现金、存货太多安全但拖累回报，太少则可能资金链断裂。现金转换周期(存货天数+应收天数−应付天数)把“钱被占用多久”量化，缩短它(快收慢付、优化库存)常能释放大量现金，比多赚一单更见效。
detailEn: Working-capital management trades liquidity against profitability: too much cash and stock is safe but drags returns, too little risks a funding break. The cash-conversion cycle (days of inventory + days of receivables − days of payables) quantifies how long cash is tied up; shortening it — collect fast, pay slow, trim stock — often frees more cash than one extra sale earns.

oneLiner: 把 ROE 拆成净利率×资产周转×权益乘数，看清回报到底靠赚钱、快转还是加杠杆。
oneLinerEn: Decompose ROE into margin × asset turnover × leverage — see whether returns come from profit, speed or borrowed money.
detail: 杜邦体系(源自通用汽车)把股东回报一层层拆开：卖得贵不贵(净利率)、资产转得快不快(周转率)、用了多少别人的钱(权益乘数)。它把“ROE 20%”这个笼统数字变成可诊断的三条路径，也暴露风险：靠杠杆堆出来的高 ROE，遇到逆风最脆弱。是连接利润表与资产负债表的桥梁。
detailEn: The DuPont system (from General Motors) breaks shareholder return layer by layer: pricing power (net margin), how fast assets turn (turnover), how much other people's money is used (the equity multiplier). It turns a bare 'ROE 20%' into three diagnosable paths and exposes risk — a high ROE built on leverage is the most fragile against a headwind. It is the bridge linking the income statement to the balance sheet.

oneLiner: 利润扣掉“占用的资本也要有回报”之后，剩下才是真正创造的价值。
oneLinerEn: Profit less a charge for the capital employed — what remains is value actually created.
detail: 斯图尔特推广的 EVA = 税后经营利润 − 资本成本×占用资本。会计利润为正不等于创造价值：若回报低于资本的机会成本，账面在赚、经济在亏。EVA 逼管理者为占用的每一元资本负责，抑制盲目扩张与“为增长而增长”，常被用来设计更贴近价值的高管激励。
detailEn: Popularised by Stewart, EVA = net operating profit after tax − (cost of capital × capital employed). Positive accounting profit is not the same as value created: if the return falls below capital's opportunity cost, the firm earns on the books while losing economically. EVA makes managers answerable for every dollar of capital tied up, curbing empire-building and 'growth for growth's sake', and is often used to tie executive pay closer to value.

oneLiner: 用少数几个能真正反映成效的量化指标，把“干得好不好”变成看得见、可追踪。
oneLinerEn: A few quantified indicators that truly reflect performance, turning 'are we doing well' into something visible and trackable.
detail: KPI 把战略与目标翻译成可衡量的关键数字，用于监控进展、发现问题、驱动改进。好的 KPI 遵循 SMART、紧扣“关键”而非堆指标——什么都能量往往意味着什么都不重要；它还要警惕古德哈特定律“一旦指标成为目标，它就不再是好指标”，否则团队会刷数字而偏离真实价值。它与 OKR 互补：OKR 定方向与野心、激发对齐，KPI 盯常态运营与达标；也呼应平衡计分卡——后者提醒别只看财务一维。
detailEn: A KPI translates strategy and goals into measurable key numbers used to monitor progress, surface problems and drive improvement. Good KPIs are SMART and stay 'key' rather than a pile of metrics — if you measure everything, it often means nothing matters; they must also guard against Goodhart's law, 'when a measure becomes a target it ceases to be a good measure', lest teams game the number and drift from real value. KPIs complement OKRs — OKRs set direction and ambition and spark alignment, KPIs watch steady-state performance and attainment — and echo the balanced scorecard, which warns against tracking the financial dimension alone.

oneLiner: 把未来的钱按贴现折算成今天值多少：NPV 为正才创造价值，IRR 是让它归零的回报率。
oneLinerEn: Discount future money to today's value — a positive NPV creates value, and the IRR is the rate that drives it to zero.
detail: 因为“今天的一元比明年的一元值钱”(时间价值)，评估投资要把未来各期现金流按要求的回报率(资本成本)贴现回今天求和，再减去初始投入得到 NPV；NPV 大于零表示收益超过资金成本、值得做，反之毁价值。IRR 则是令 NPV 归零的那个内在回报率，越高越好、须高于资本成本。它比“多久回本”更讲道理，因为它顾到全部现金流与货币时间价值；但两者都依赖贴现率估计，对非常规现金流(正负交替)IRR 可能多个或失真，此时以 NPV 为准。
detailEn: Because a dollar today beats a dollar next year (time value), appraising an investment discounts each future cash flow back to now at the required return (cost of capital), sums them and subtracts the outlay to get NPV; NPV over zero means returns beat the cost of money and it is worth doing, below zero it destroys value. The IRR is the rate that sets NPV to zero — the higher the better, and it must exceed the cost of capital. It beats 'payback period' by honouring all cash flows and the time value of money, but both lean on the discount-rate estimate, and for unconventional cash flows that flip sign the IRR can be multiple or misleading — there, trust NPV.

oneLiner: 选了 A，成本就是被放弃的最好那个 B——真代价常在“你没做的另一件事”里。
oneLinerEn: Choose A and the cost is the best B you forwent — the real price usually sits in the thing you did not do.
detail: 机会成本指为得到某选择而放弃的最佳替代方案的价值，它不进账本却决定取舍：自建团队的钱若投进主业更赚，那“更赚”才是自建的隐藏成本；老板亲自盯生产线的“工资”按他别处能创造的价值算，常高于雇人。它也提醒：已花的钱是沉没成本、不该左右未来，而“用满资源”不等于“用对资源”。在决策树、投资评估与资源配置里，把隐形的“次优选项”显式算进去，才不至于用“看起来没花钱”骗自己。
detailEn: Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative you give up to choose something; it never books as an expense yet it decides trade-offs — if cash spent building an in-house team would earn more in the core business, that 'more' is the hidden cost of building; the owner's time supervising a line is priced by the value they would create elsewhere, often above hiring someone. It also warns that money already spent is a sunk cost that should not sway the future, and that using every resource is not using resources well. In decision trees, investment appraisal and allocation, making the invisible runner-up explicit keeps you from fooling yourself that a choice costs nothing.
